name: Clube de Fado
seoTitle: Clube de Fado: €78 Dinner and Fado Near the Ship
tagline: A fado house below the Sé, founded by a guitarist, six minutes on foot from the cruise terminal.

description.short: Clube de Fado is a fado house on Rua de São João da Praça, below Lisbon Cathedral, opened in 1995 by the guitarist Mário Pacheco. One set menu at €78 includes the fado; the first set starts at 20:30.
description.full:
Clube de Fado only fits a port day if your ship stays in Lisbon into the evening or overnight. It is an evening venue: the kitchen opens at 19:30, the first fado set starts at 20:30 and the night runs until about 01:00. Check your all-aboard time before you book.

Getting there is easy. The house is on Rua de São João da Praça, the street that curves round below the Sé, about 400 m and six minutes on foot from the terminal: walk west along the riverside avenue and turn up into lower Alfama behind the cathedral. Coming back late, the walk is short and mostly downhill, or a taxi takes a few minutes.

There is one menu, at €78 per person (2026): couvert, starter, main course and dessert, with the fado included. Drinks are extra; wine by the glass starts at €9. The seafood cataplana adds €40 per person. Book online (free, up to 10 people); the room is small and evenings fill in advance, especially in summer and at weekends.

Arrive between 19:30 and 20:00 so the first courses are on the table before the singing starts. Sets alternate with the courses. When someone stands to sing, service stops and the room goes silent: that is the house's one rule, and it covers phones too. If you have to be back on board by about 22:30, you will hear the first sets but not the full night, so tell staff when you sit down.

The house was opened in January 1995 by the guitarist Mário Pacheco, who accompanied Amália Rodrigues. It is a dinner venue with professional musicians, not a casual tasca where neighbours take turns to sing, and it is priced accordingly. The house also has a petiscos menu (€4–20) for people arriving after dinner; ask when booking whether a later, lighter visit is possible.
description.history: Clube de Fado opened in January 1995. Its founder, Mário Pacheco, is a Portuguese guitar player who accompanied Amália Rodrigues, Alfredo Marceneiro and Carlos do Carmo and has composed for Mariza, Camané and Mísia. He set out to build a house around the music rather than a restaurant that added fado later. It occupies part of a building more than 300 years old on Rua de São João da Praça, which runs round the cathedral, and stone arches divide the dining room into alcoves. In 2006 the Casa da Imprensa awarded it its Prémio Casa de Fado. Fado itself took shape in 19th-century Lisbon, in neighbourhoods such as Alfama and Mouraria.
description.significance: UNESCO inscribed fado on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2011, and evening fado houses are where most visitors hear it live. Clube de Fado is one of the established professional houses in Alfama, run by a musician, with singers performing between the tables rather than on a raised stage. For a cruise passenger it is also one of the closest fado houses to the ship.

address.street: Rua de São João da Praça 94

directions.general: Located in Alfama's winding streets, near Lisbon Cathedral (Sé) and São Jorge Castle
directions.fromCruisePort: About 400 m and 6 minutes on foot from the Jardim do Tabaco terminal, just behind the cathedral in lower Alfama. A taxi back to the ship after the late show takes minutes.
directions.publicTransport: Tram 28 to Sé Cathedral, then 5-minute walk. Bus 737 to Sé. Metro: Terreiro do Paço or Santa Apolónia (Blue line) then 10-15 minute uphill walk.
directions.parking: Very limited street parking in Alfama. Best parking at Portas do Sol or Sé Cathedral area (5-10 minute walk).

seasonal.notes: Kitchen opens at 19:30; first fado set at 20:30. Sets alternate with the courses until closing.

admissionPrices.notes: No separate entry ticket: the €78 set menu (couvert, starter, main course and dessert, 2026) includes the fado. Drinks are extra (wine by the glass from €9). Seafood cataplana +€40 per person. A petiscos menu (€4–20) is available for later arrivals. Children's prices are not published; ask when booking.

visitingInformation.averageVisitDuration: 2.5–3 hours for dinner and the first sets; up to 5 hours if you stay until closing
visitingInformation.bestTimeToVisit: Arrive 19:30–20:00 so you have eaten your starter before the first set at 20:30. Book ahead for summer and weekend evenings.
visitingInformation.adviceForVisitors: Book online; it is free and immediate for up to 10 people. Stay silent during each fado and keep phones away; talk and order between sets. Drinks are not included in the €78 menu. Groups of more than 10 should phone or email.

cruisePassengerInfo.timeNeededFromPort: 3–4 hours for dinner and several sets, plus about 6 minutes' walk each way
cruisePassengerInfo.accessibility: Six minutes on foot from the terminal, ending on a sloping Alfama street. The house is in an old building with stone arches; contact it before booking to ask about steps and access.
tips: Check your all-aboard time first: fado starts at 20:30 and the night runs to about 01:00.
Book online at clubedefado.pt (free and immediate for up to 10 people); larger groups book by phone on +351 218 852 704 or by email.
Budget €78 per person for the set menu with fado, plus drinks: wine by the glass starts at €9.
Arrive between 19:30 and 20:00 so you have eaten your starter before the first set.
Stay silent during each fado and keep phones away; service pauses while someone sings.
From the terminal, walk west along the river and up behind the Sé: about six minutes. Late at night a taxi back takes a few minutes.
If your ship leaves before evening, the Fado Museum on Largo do Chafariz de Dentro, a few minutes from the terminal, is open Tuesday to Sunday, 10:00–18:00 (€5).
The set menu has vegetarian main courses; mention allergies when you book.

highlights: Founded in 1995 by the guitarist Mário Pacheco, who accompanied Amália Rodrigues
One set menu at €78 with the fado included (drinks extra)
Fado sung between the tables, with no raised stage
Stone-arched dining room in a building over 300 years old, below the Sé
First set at 20:30; sets alternate with courses until about 01:00
About six minutes' walk from the cruise terminal

accessibility.mobilityNotes: Old building with stone arches and a sloping street outside. Contact the house before booking about steps and seating if you have limited mobility.
